title: How to Make a Quick Herb‑Packed Chimichurri for Grilled Steak
meta_description: Level up your grilled steak with this quick herb-packed chimichurri recipe. Learn the secret to fast chopping and the best fresh ingredients to use.
html:
There is nothing quite like a perfectly seared ribeye or flank steak, but the meat is only half the story. To truly elevate a grilled steak, you need a bright, acidic, and punchy topping. That is where a classic Argentinian-style sauce comes in. If you are short on time but want maximum flavor, this quick herb-packed chimichurri recipe delivers a zesty contrast to rich, fatty meats in under ten minutes.

The secret to a great chimichurri isn't a food processor—which often turns the herbs into a muddy paste—but a coarse, hand-cut texture. You want distinct bits of garlic, parsley, and oregano that pop in your mouth. Here is how to get that professional result without spending an hour at the cutting board.

The Ingredients for a Quick Herb-Packed Chimichurri Recipe

To get that signature balance of earthiness and acidity, focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients. Avoid dried parsley at all costs; it lacks the brightness required for this sauce. You will need:

  • Fresh Flat-Leaf Parsley: The backbone of the sauce.
  • Fresh Oregano or Cilantro: Oregano is traditional, but cilantro adds a great citrusy note.
  • Fresh Garlic: Three to four cloves, minced fine.
  • Red Wine Vinegar: This provides the sharp tang that cuts through the steak's fat.
  • Extra Virgin Olive Oil: Use a good quality oil to emulsify the herbs.
  • Red Pepper Flakes: For a subtle, warming heat.
  • Kosher Salt and Black Pepper: To taste.

Streamlining the Prep with Herb Scissors

The most tedious part of any herb-heavy recipe is the chopping. If you've ever spent ten minutes meticulously dicing parsley only to find the knife blade clogged with greens, you know the struggle. This is where the right tool makes a massive difference in your kitchen workflow.

To speed up this process, I use Herb Scissors. These five-blade herb shears allow you to mince cilantro, chives, and basil in one snip, effectively quintupling your chopping speed. Instead of a knife and board, you can snip your parsley and oregano directly into your mixing bowl. The included cleaning comb makes it easy to clear out the stuck herbs, so you aren't fighting with the blades between ingredients.

Step-by-Step Instructions for the Perfect Sauce

Once your ingredients are gathered and your tools are ready, follow these simple steps to assemble your sauce:

First, finely mince your garlic. I prefer to smash it with the side of a knife first to release the oils before chopping it into tiny bits. Place the garlic in a small bowl and stir in the red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper.

Next, focus on the greens. Using your Herb Scissors, snip a large handful of fresh parsley and a smaller amount of oregano directly into the bowl. Because the five blades create a consistent, fine cut, you get a uniform texture that distributes evenly throughout the sauce.

Whisk in the red wine vinegar first, letting the acid macerate the garlic and herbs for a minute. Finally, slowly stir in the olive oil until the sauce reaches a spoonable consistency. Taste and adjust the salt—remember, the salt is what wakes up the flavor of the herbs.

Pairing Your Chimichurri with Grilled Steak

While this sauce is versatile, it is designed for the grill. For the best results, use a high-heat sear on a New York strip or a skirt steak. Let the meat rest for at least five to ten minutes after taking it off the heat; this ensures the juices redistribute and don't wash away your sauce.

Spoon the chimichurri generously over the sliced meat just before serving. The cold, acidic sauce hitting the hot, salty crust of the steak creates a temperature and flavor contrast that is addictive. If you have leftovers, the sauce keeps well in the fridge for up to a week, though the color may fade slightly as the vinegar preserves the herbs.

Pro Tips for Better Flavor

If you find the sauce too sharp, add a pinch of brown sugar or honey to mellow out the vinegar. If you want a deeper, smokier profile, try substituting a tablespoon of the olive oil with a smoked paprika oil.

For those who prefer a thicker consistency, you can add a teaspoon of Dijon mustard. This acts as a stabilizer and helps the sauce cling to the meat more effectively. No matter which variation you choose, using a tool like Herb Scissors ensures the herbs are cut cleanly without bruising, preserving the vibrant green color and fresh taste of your creation.

FAQ

Can I use a blender for this recipe?

You can, but it is not recommended. Blenders tend to over-process the herbs, turning them into a puree. A hand-cut texture, achieved with a knife or Herb Scissors, provides a much better mouthfeel and keeps the flavors distinct.

How long does homemade chimichurri last?

Stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator, it will stay fresh for about 5 to 7 days. The olive oil acts as a natural preservative, though the parsley may darken over time.

What can I use if I don't have red wine vinegar?

Apple cider vinegar is the best substitute as it has a similar acidity. If you don't have any vinegar, fresh lemon juice can work, though the flavor will be more citrusy and less pungent than the traditional version.
